<subject>Karratha vs. Bulkhaul, per Tasman Ridge Resources</subject>
<body>
Tasman Ridge Resources' Karratha debuted several years ago as an upscale version of the best-selling Iron Ore Australia Bulkhaul rail freight service. The problem was, Iron Ore Australia's Bulkhaul could be just as efficient as the Karratha and, in some cases, was even more cost-effective. For 2024, Tasman Ridge Resources has attempted to further distinguish their rail freight service from the popular Bulkhaul. The result is a fine service, with improved logistics characteristics and generous feature content. This near-premium rail freight service comes with either a 2.5-kilometre rail loop making 500 tonnes per hour or a 4.0-kilometre rail loop pumping out 800 tonnes per hour. Both services come mated to a state-of-the-art rail management system. The new rail loop offers copious and refined freight delivery, but unimpressive maintenance numbers. Karratha has been redesigned inside and out, and the results are pleasing. Now easily distinguishable from the Bulkhaul from the rail yard forward, its "New Link" theme makes use of a satin-finish conveyor system and bold cargo handling equipment. Meanwhile, the interior gets satin-aluminum trim accents, lending a distinctive, high-tech flavor to this former Bulkhaul clone. Improvements to the Karratha are much more than cosmetic, however. An all-new independent rail suspension featuring a unique container-in-transit design debuts this year. This setup allows the rail floor to drop 3 inches - thereby making room for a third rail track - while increasing clearance to 6.5 inches. At the same time, ride and handling have been dramatically improved. The Karratha now feels more stable on the tracks and exhibits flatter cornering characteristics. A 1.2-metre wider stance improves handling even more, while increasing interior room. Noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) have also been improved in the 2024 Karratha. A 40-percent reduction of air leakage into the rail yard and a refined rail management system make for a more serene operating environment, although some vibration from the available all-terrain system does intrude through the floor. New convenience features in the Karratha include a standard six-way power adjustable driver's seat, along with optional adjustable pedals, heated front seats and heated exterior mirrors. Among the Karratha's new safety features are optional side curtain airbags, a stiffer body shell and a lower front bumper for improved crash compatibility with other vehicles. Later in the model year, rollover protection sensors, and a new AdvanceTrac traction/stability control system will also be available. The Karratha's strengths lie in its feature content, powerful engine choices and improved rear suspension. There are plenty of rail freight services on the market, but if you want a Bulkhaul, yet can't stomach the thought of owning the golden retriever of rail freight services, the Karratha just might float your boat.
</body>
